body:
Synced folders handle table links and long documents better, and a folder no longer leaves stale refused edge writes behind.

### Server
- **Added:** `GET /` now reports `max_request_bytes`, the largest request the server accepts, so a device can tell before it sends.

### CLI
- **Added:** A file too large for the server's request limit is held on your device with a message giving both sizes, and goes once it is smaller or the limit rises. The other files in the same push are still delivered.
- **Changed:** The field a type names as its body field now holds up to 1,000,000 characters by default, so a long Markdown document fits in one item. Other text fields keep 100,000.
- **Fixed:** A link in a table cell such as `[[Plan\|Label]]` now links to `Plan` with the label `Label`, in a table, a quote or a callout, instead of reporting that nothing matched.
- **Fixed:** A synced file is no longer uploaded half-written when the server is slow to answer.
- **Fixed:** A deleted file is no longer left unsent after the watch goes to rest during the five-second rename grace.
- **Fixed:** Refused edge writes that the folder has since satisfied are cleared, instead of piling up with each save of the file.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.64...v0.0.65

A folder's local copy now gives freed disk space back after it shrinks.

### Core
- **Added:** A folder's local copy gives freed space back to the disk after a large shrink, so a copy that went from hundreds of rows to a few no longer keeps its old size. The folder watch reports `Reclaimed` or `ReclaimFailed` when it happens.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.63...v0.0.64

Folders ask before taking in a large drop of new files, can hold files outside their query, and keep far less in a device's working copy.

### Server
- **Added:** `GET /items` and `GET /items/stats` take `beneath=<item id>` to list or count an item and everything below it by `parent-of`.
- **Added:** the `system.folder` type has `addition_threshold`, `outside_query` and `full_pass_interval_seconds` settings. A value out of range is refused with `validation_error`.

### CLI
- **Added:** a folder asks before taking in a large drop of new files, as it already does for a large removal. `marfa folders confirm` sends the files held back. Set the limit with `--addition-threshold`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/folder-safeguards)
- **Added:** `--outside-query hold` on `marfa folders create` and `change` keeps new files that the folder's query would not show on disk, unsent. `marfa folders status` and `folders unmatched` list them.
- **Added:** `--full-pass-interval-seconds` sets how often a folder watch reads every file in case the system missed an event. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/keep-folders-running)
- **Changed:** a watch's full pass runs every 10 minutes instead of every 60 seconds.
- **Fixed:** `marfa folders autostart on` now carries your telemetry settings into the watch started at login.
- **Fixed:** a new folder file whose `state` the folder's query does not hold stays in the folder and is counted as unmatched, instead of being removed on the next pull.
- **Fixed:** a folder still filling its copy no longer shows `settings_invalid` or `unavailable`.

### Core
- **Changed:** a folder's working copy holds only the items the folder shows, and a `beneath` folder holds only its subtree. In one test a folder of 2,134 notes went from 27,626 rows to 3,139, and its store from 160 MiB to 36 MiB. An existing copy shrinks on upgrade without touching unsent writes.
- **Changed:** on Apple platforms a pull writes files with a barrier flush and one full flush at the end, which is faster and still durable when the pull reports success.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.62...v0.0.63

A Marfa server now reports memory, CPU and storage figures once a day, and `marfa metrics` shows the same figures.

### Server
- **Added:** A server where error reporting is configured sends one `marfa server report` event to PostHog shortly after start and every 24 hours after. It carries 16 figures (memory, CPU, uptime, database size, row counts and the release) and no item content, IDs, paths or host names. Unset the PostHog settings or turn error reporting off to stop it.
- **Added:** `GET /metrics` gains a `process` block (release, memory, peak memory, heap, CPU, uptime) and a `storage` block (database and log file sizes, row counts of items, versions, the event log and the audit log, and when they were counted). Row counts are taken about once an hour in the background, so a request never waits for them.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa metrics` shows the new `process` and `storage` blocks. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/cli)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.61...v0.0.62

The server stays responsive while a large bulk page is written and gives memory back afterward, and `marfa export` now waits for the archive of a large instance.

### Server
- **Fixed:** A large `POST /items/bulk` or `POST /edges/bulk` page no longer stops the server from answering other requests. Reads during a 5,000-entry page answer in milliseconds, and a single write may wait for the page to finish.
- **Fixed:** A best-effort bulk page no longer slows down as it goes: 5,000 entries take about 8 seconds instead of 20 to 53, and memory grows by about 200 MB instead of more than 1 GB.
- **Fixed:** After bulk work the server hands the memory back, so resident memory returns near its starting size within seconds instead of staying near its peak.
- **Fixed:** Creating a `parent-of` or other cycle-risk edge is much faster on a large store; the check for a leaf target on 100,000 edges falls from about 47 ms to about 0.05 ms. Which edges are refused does not change.

### CLI
- **Fixed:** `marfa export --format archive` waits up to 30 minutes for the archive of a large instance and reports on standard error every 15 seconds that it is still preparing it, instead of failing after 90 seconds. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/export-and-restore)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.60...v0.0.61

Folder sync is faster: a watched folder sends an edit to the server sooner, and a first sync of a large folder drains its queue much quicker.

### Core
- **Changed:** A first push of a large folder is about three times faster in our test (547 s down to 160 s for 33,882 writes), because a file's links are now queued in one step and the queue no longer slows as it grows.
- **Changed:** An edit in a watched folder reaches the server sooner (median 1.46 s, down from 2.16 s on a folder of 10,000 notes), because the watch no longer runs a second pass that finds nothing.
- **Fixed:** A watched folder now retries a placement that was refused for a key, within a minute of that key becoming readable again.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.59...v0.0.60

Synced folders are much faster on large instances: a one-file edit reaches the server in about 4.5 seconds instead of 15.7 on a 10,000-note folder.

### Server
- **Added:** `POST /items/titles` returns the items titled by up to 200 names in one request.
- **Changed:** The server keeps a folded title key for each item (database migration 10), so a title lookup no longer reads every item. The update runs once at first start, after the backup copy described in "Before you upgrade".

### CLI
- **Changed:** A synced folder resolves a scan's `[[links]]` in a few requests, not several per name.
- **Changed:** A folder's watch reads only the items a change reaches, and clears answered writes from its queue, so a quiet folder stays quiet and uses less CPU.

### Core
- **Fixed:** Queuing an edge in a folder scan no longer slows down as the copy grows.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.58...v0.0.59

A working copy now refuses duplicate and cardinality-breaking edges before it queues them, and can check an edge move in advance.

### Core
- **Added:** A working copy refuses an edge write that the server would refuse as a duplicate or because an end already holds its one edge, so you learn of it at once instead of when the write is sent. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/write-in-a-working-copy)
- **Added:** You can check whether moving an edge's end would be refused, without queuing anything, to disable a drop target before the person tries it. The Swift and Node bindings gain `checkEdgeMove`.
- **Changed:** An edge refusal from a working copy now carries the same `details` the server gives for the same write, so an app can tell a duplicate (`details.constraint` is `duplicate`) from a full end (`cardinality`). The Swift `MarfaError.validation` case gains a `details` value, and the thrown Node error gains a `details` property. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/api-reference/errors)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa device edges check-move <ID> (--source <ID> | --target <ID>)` answers what the matching edge move would, and queues nothing.
- **Changed:** The error output carries the refusal's details in `error.server.details`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.57...v0.0.58

Deleting a file in a synced folder now sticks, and a quiet folder watch rests between passes.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A file you delete in a synced folder now goes to the bin with its item, even when the file held a link name that matched no item, matched more than one, or could not be looked up, or when the server had refused an edit to it. Before, the next pull could write the file back. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/troubleshooting/folders)
- **Fixed:** A folder watch with nothing to do pulls at most once a minute instead of on every tick, until something changes.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.56...v0.0.57

Highlights are now named after the item they come from, folder watches follow upgrades, and several commands and Catalog descriptions read better.

### Server
- **Changed:** A highlight is named after its source, such as "Excerpt from Thinking, Fast and Slow", and its passage shows as the preview, so lists no longer show a paragraph where a name belongs. A type can now say its body is not its name. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/display-hints)
- **Changed:** The descriptions of the shipped types, fields and edge types are rewritten to say what each is for. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/types)

### CLI
- **Added:** `--state` on `marfa items list`, `marfa search` and `marfa export` takes a list of states, repeated or comma-separated. `any` stands alone. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/cli)
- **Fixed:** A folder watch that starts at login restarts on the new build after an upgrade, so it no longer runs the old version until you log out. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/troubleshooting/folders)
- **Fixed:** `marfa server install` repeats the warning to keep `marfa.env` until an install has succeeded.  [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/install)

### Core
- **Fixed:** A folder pull goes on when the server refuses to show one attached file, and reports that file on its document instead of stopping.
- **Fixed:** A watch started right after `marfa folders add --yes` no longer ends on its first pass while the folder's copy is still hydrating.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.55...v0.0.56

Fixes a v0.0.53 regression that stopped a signed-in device from hydrating, and makes `marfa folders status` show every file that needs attention.

### CLI
- **Added:** A folder default edge that the server refused now has its own flag, `default_edge_refused`, in `marfa folders status` and in a scan. The file itself is reported as sent, with the reason the edge was not applied, instead of being counted as held.
- **Fixed:** `marfa folders status` lists every file that carries a flag, reason or warning, whatever its status.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A signed-in device hydrates again. In v0.0.53 the check that decides whether to hydrate was refused by the server with `validation_error`, "Conditional item pages require include=metadata".

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.54...v0.0.55

Connectors can now mark items as read only, and a server reports its exception errors to PostHog with just its PostHog settings.

### Server
- **Added:** Every item now carries `read_only`, which is `true` when a connector that owns the item will put back any edit made in Marfa, so an app can show it as locked. Marfa still accepts the edit. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/connector)
- **Added:** A connector can list the types it holds read only in `read_only_types` when it registers. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/connector)
- **Added:** After an upgrade, `GET /types` lists any stored type whose field conflicts with a shipped type under `conflicts`, and the server logs a warning at start. The type's items stay readable and listable, and the report clears once the type agrees. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/define-a-type)
- **Changed:** The server sends exception reports to PostHog when `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` and `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` are set, without an OTLP endpoint. `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` now turns off the server's traces, logs and exception reports; an instance that already sets it sends none. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Fixed:** A client that drops an upload partway is no longer logged as a server fault, reported or answered 500. Background job logs keep the database error code.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.53...v0.0.54

Passkeys now show when each was last used, and working copies and synced folders fix several cases where a link, an edge or a removal came out wrong.

### Server
- **Added:** Each owner passkey shows when it was last used, so you can tell which ones are still in use. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/sign-in-as-the-owner)

### CLI
- **Fixed:** A command that fails reports the failure to error tracking when only the PostHog settings are set, without an OTLP endpoint.

### Core
- **Added:** An app can remove fetched files without changing the file budget. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/keep-files-on-a-device)
- **Changed:** A working copy fills 500 items a page, so a first sync of a large library takes fewer requests.
- **Fixed:** A synced folder rewrites `[[links]]` to a note when the note is retitled.
- **Fixed:** A synced folder reads an escaped pipe in a table cell, and Markdown escapes such as `\_` in an embed path, so the embed finds its file.
- **Fixed:** A folder's default edge that Marfa refused stays visible and is tried again.
- **Fixed:** A row or edge you removed on a device stays gone until the server's removal event arrives, instead of reappearing for a moment.
- **Fixed:** A create that sets edges now reads all of them as it settles.
- **Fixed:** A cleared time stays cleared when an unsent create with a key lands on an item the device already holds.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.52...v0.0.53

Attachments and comments now belong to the item they are on and go to the bin with it, an embed in a note no longer attaches its file, and each source has a name.

### Server
- **Added:** Attachments and comments are parts of their item. A part goes to the bin with the last item it belongs to and comes back when any of them is restored. A registered edge type can make its items parts with the new `with-hosts` delete mode, and the filter `part eq true` lets a list leave parts out. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/edges)
- **Added:** The `comments-on` edge links a comment to the item it is on.
- **Added:** The `excerpt-of` edge links a highlight, quote or clip to the item it was taken from.
- **Added:** Each source, such as `github`, has a readable name and an optional mark, and stats can count items by source. Names and marks are in the API, MCP, the CLI and archives.
- **Changed:** A `references` edge now means only a mention: a link or embed in an item's text, or a link a system makes. Use `excerpt-of` for an excerpt.

### Core
- **Changed:** An embed in a note's body makes a `references` edge to the file instead of attaching it, so editing the body never decides whether the file belongs to the note or goes to the bin with it. Attach a file to keep it with the note. Working copies and folders read their bodies again once to add the references. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/handle-files)
- **Added:** A working copy answers the `part` filter and names a part without a title after its item, as the server does, so lists and saved views read the same offline.
- **Fixed:** A synced folder resolves a link to a note that did not exist yet on the next sync after that note is made, instead of waiting until you edit the file. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/sync-a-folder)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.51...v0.0.52

A folder you remove and add again now takes back its embedded files instead of copying them, and deleting a file such a folder found on disk now deletes its item.

### Core
- **Fixed:** When you remove a synced folder and add it again, the first sync takes back the images and other files its notes embed as the items they were. Before, it sent each one as a new item and wrote the original beside it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/folder-safeguards)
- **Fixed:** Deleting or binning a file that a folder added again took back now sends its item to the bin, as it does for any other file in the folder.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.50...v0.0.51
